blocks.t: A Consequence for Root Finding We call a solution of the equation ƒ(x) = 0 a root of the equation or zero of the function ƒ. The Intermediate Value Theorem tells us that if ƒ is continuous, then any interval on which ƒ changes sign contains a zero of the function.

In practical terms, when we see the graph of a continuous function cross the horizon- tal axis on a computer screen, we know it is not stepping across. There really is a point where the function’s value is zero.
